To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the co-expression of cell cycle regulator genes At-Cycd2 and At-Cdc27a from Arabdopsis thaliana with TMV vector in N. benthaniana results in an enhanced accumulation of the foreign protein.
co-infiltration of a TMV-based vector and the At-CycDs and At-CDCs from A. thaliana enhanced the accumulation of heterologous proteins in N. benthaniana leaves.
co-infiltration of the TMV-gfp with binary expression vectors carrying cell cycle checkpoint genes from Arabidopsis resulted in enhanced GFP accumulation in agroinfiltrated N. benthamina leaves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and optimization of a plant-based expression system for the production of recombinant antibodies and proteins.
a new approach for the improvement of foreign protein production in plants.
the enhancement of transient expression systems for the production of foreign proteins in N. benthaniana.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cell cycle regulator genes At-Cycd2 and At-Cdc27a enhance the accumulation of foreign proteins in agroinfiltrated Nicotiana benthmaniana leaves.
the co-infiltration of the cell cycle checkpoint gene At-CycD and At-CDC with a TMV based expression vector enhances foreign protein accumulation in N. benthaniana leaves.
the plant cell cycle regulator At-CycD3a and At-CDC25a genes are able to increase the transient protein production in N.benthamiana leaves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the co-infiltration of the cell cycle checkpoint regulator genes At-Cyc2 and At-Cdc27a in combination with a viral vector for protein delivery enhances the accumulation of heterologous protein in N. bentahamiana leaves.

co-delivery of cell cycle regulators with a TMV based expression vector enhances heterologous protein accumulation in the host plant N. benthamian.
The main takeaway from our work is that
co-expression of the cell cycle regulators CycD2 and/or CDC27a with the TMV vector enhances the accumulation of foreign proteins in agroinfiltrated N. benthamianaleaves.
cell cycle regulator genes from plants can enhance the production of heterologous proteins in plants.
the cell cycle regulators CycD2 and CDC27a from A. thaliana can be used as a tool to enhance the transient expression of recombinant protein in the model plant N. benthamian.
